brief.t: Started in Pune in 1987 as Bajaj Auto Finance, lending for Bajaj two- and three-wheelers; now a large consumer and business lender of the Bajaj group, run under the Bajaj Finserv brand.

Rajeev Jain has led it since 2007. He became Vice Chairman in April 2025 when Anup Saha was made MD, but Saha resigned in July 2025 and Jain is again Vice Chairman & MD (term to March 2028). Sanjiv Bajaj is Chairman.
FY 2025-26 (consolidated): profit ₹19,332 crore (+15%) after one-time charges; AUM crossed ₹5 lakh crore (₹5,09,975 crore, +22%).
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026): consolidated profit ₹6,367 crore (+29%), AUM ₹5.85 lakh crore (+26%), 12.9 crore customers.
In Nov 2026 it raised about ₹17,500 crore of fresh capital: an ₹11,700 crore QIP and ₹5,800 crore of warrants to promoter Bajaj Finserv.

timeline.t: Incorporated in Pune as Bajaj Auto Finance, financing Bajaj vehicles.
Rajeev Jain (ex-GE, American Express, AIG) joined as CEO.
RBI stopped loans via its eCOM and Insta EMI Card for gaps in loan fact sheets; curbs lifted in May 2024.
Subsidiary Bajaj Housing Finance listed on the stock market after a ₹6,560 crore IPO.
MD Anup Saha resigned; Rajeev Jain became Vice Chairman & MD again.
Raised about ₹17,500 crore through a QIP and warrants to Bajaj Finserv.

model.how: Bajaj Finance borrows money from banks, bond investors and public fixed deposits, and lends it to millions of people and small businesses at higher rates. It is known for EMI loans at shops, personal loans, business loans, and now gold loans and microfinance; its subsidiary Bajaj Housing Finance gives home loans. Huge customer data helps it cross-sell more products to the same customers.
flow: Raises money: bank loans, bonds, fixed deposits
Lends: EMI, personal, business, gold, home loans

points: RBI lists Bajaj Finance as an 'Upper Layer' NBFC, so it faces stricter, bank-like rules.
RBI acts on weak customer disclosure: in Nov 2023 it paused two Bajaj Finance digital products until fixes were made.
Unsecured small-business (MSME) loans came under stress in 2025, making the company cut growth guidance and slow that book.

people_changes.t: Apr 2025: Anup Kumar Saha became MD and Rajeev Jain moved to Vice Chairman. Saha resigned in Jul 2025 (personal reasons); Jain re-designated Vice Chairman & MD from 22 Jul 2025.
Senior managers including Harjeet Toor, Sidhant Dadwal and Manish Jain were made Deputy CEOs in 2025.

points.t: Consolidated net profit ₹6,367 cr, up 29% from ₹4,948 cr a year earlier.
AUM ₹5,84,624 cr (+26%); customer franchise 128.85 million (+16%); 13.45 million new loans.
Gross NPA 1.06%, Net NPA 0.42%; capital adequacy 20.33%. Included a ₹337 cr extra provision for economic risks.

numbers.say: Bajaj Finance grew profit 29% to ₹6,367 crore last quarter, with loans under management up 26% to ₹5.85 lakh crore and Gross NPA near 1%.

rivals.note: Competes with big NBFCs in consumer, vehicle and gold loans, and with private banks in personal and business loans.

network.local: Headquartered in Pune. Its EMI loans are sold at shops and dealers across India, so many roles are in sales, partner management and collections in cities and small towns.

employer.note: 71,613 full-time staff in March 2026 (annual report) and 73,261 in June 2026 (Q1 FY27 coverage). The group also uses many fixed-term contract staff.

csr.t: Bajaj Finance contributes to 'Bajaj Beyond', the Bajaj Group's ₹5,000 crore, five-year CSR commitment focused on youth (skills) and children.

glossary.NBFC: Non-Banking Financial Company: a lender regulated by the RBI that gives loans but cannot take savings or current account deposits like a bank.
glossary.AUM: Assets Under Management: the total loans an NBFC has given out and not yet been repaid. The main size measure for a lender.
glossary.Disbursements: New loans paid out to customers in a period.
glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The company's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on borrowings. A lender's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of loans or interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Loans not repaid for 90+ days (called 'Stage 3' loans by NBFCs), as a % of all loans.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.Stage 3 assets: Loans that have stopped paying for 90+ days. NBFCs report Gross and Net Stage 3, similar to banks' NPA.
glossary.Credit cost: Money set aside for bad loans, as a % of average loans. Lower means fewer losses.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The lender's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires NBFCs to keep at least 15%.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Borrowings: Money an NBFC raises from banks, bonds (NCDs), commercial paper and, for some, public deposits, to lend onward.
glossary.Cost of funds: The average interest an NBFC pays on its borrowings. NBFCs usually pay more than banks, so a strong credit rating matters.
glossary.Credit rating: An agency's grade (e.g. AAA) of how safely a company can repay debt. Higher ratings mean cheaper borrowing.
glossary.Upper Layer NBFC: The largest and most important NBFCs, named by the RBI under its scale-based rules. They face bank-like rules and must list on the stock market within 3 years.
glossary.Return on assets: Net profit as a % of average total assets. Shows how well a lender earns on what it owns.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates banks and NBFCs in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before giving a loan.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that lenders serve.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like insurance or a second loan) to an existing customer.
glossary.Co-lending: A bank and an NBFC lending together: the NBFC finds and services the borrower, the bank funds most of the loan.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first sells its shares to the public.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Customer franchise: All customers who have ever taken a product from the company. Bajaj Finance uses it as its main customer count.
glossary.Consolidated: Figures for the company together with its subsidiaries (for Bajaj Finance: Bajaj Housing Finance and Bajaj Broking). 'Standalone' means the parent company alone.
glossary.QIP: Qualified Institutions Placement: a listed company sells new shares quickly to large investors such as mutual funds and insurers to raise capital.
glossary.Warrants: A right to buy new shares later at a fixed price. Part of the money is paid now and the rest when converted into shares.
glossary.Management overlay: An extra provision a lender sets aside for possible future risks (for example, a slowing economy), on top of normal bad-loan provisions.
glossary.Consumer durable loan: A small EMI loan to buy items like phones, TVs or fridges, usually given at the shop counter.

Finance.tip: Know AUM, Gross vs Net Stage 3, cost of funds and credit cost, and the company's latest profit.

Marketing.tip: Think about reaching first-time and small-town borrowers through dealers, branches and mobile.

HR.tip: NBFCs hire many field and branch staff. Ideas to cut early attrition and train people fast will impress.

Sales.tip: Expect role-play: 'Sell me a two-wheeler loan' or 'Convince a shopkeeper to take a business loan.'

Operations.tip: Show you understand KYC, loan turnaround time, collections and how automation reduces errors.

Finance.q: FY26 profit was ₹19,332 cr but also ₹20,689 cr is quoted. Why two numbers?
Finance.a: ₹20,689 cr is before one-time items such as extra loan-loss provisions and the new Labour Codes charge; ₹19,332 cr (+15%) is the reported consolidated profit after them.

Finance.q: What is the difference between consolidated and standalone profit here?
Finance.a: Consolidated includes Bajaj Housing Finance and Bajaj Broking; standalone is Bajaj Finance alone (₹17,804 cr in FY26).

Finance.q: Why raise ₹17,500 cr when profits are strong?
Finance.a: Fast loan growth needs more capital to keep capital adequacy comfortable; management said the money is mainly for growth.

Marketing.q: How does Bajaj Finance reach so many new customers?
Marketing.a: Through EMI financing at 2.4 lakh+ shops and dealers, apps and web, then cross-selling more loans, cards and insurance.

Marketing.q: How would you market gold loans for Bajaj Finance?
Marketing.a: Target existing customers in small towns, stress quick approval, safe storage and clear monthly interest options.

HR.q: How would you keep 70,000+ staff motivated during leadership changes?
HR.a: Clear communication from the VC & MD and Deputy CEOs, stable targets, fast promotions for performers and training on AI tools.

Sales.q: Sell a Bajaj Finance EMI loan to a customer buying a phone.
Sales.a: Find the budget, show the monthly EMI, explain the tenure and charges clearly, and close at the counter.

Operations.q: How can AI improve loan operations?
Operations.a: Faster KYC and document checks, chatbots for service and better collection calls; the company already uses AI bots in service and lending.

Other.q: What do you know about Bajaj Finance?
Other.a: A Pune-based NBFC started in 1987, led by Vice Chairman & MD Rajeev Jain and Chairman Sanjiv Bajaj, with ₹5.85 lakh cr AUM and ₹6,367 cr profit in Q2 FY27.

interview.why_us: Bajaj Finance began as a small vehicle-finance company in Pune and now serves about 12.9 crore customers with over ₹5.8 lakh crore of loans. It keeps bad loans near 1% while growing fast, and it is using AI across sales, service and collections. I want to learn how a data-driven lender works at this scale and contribute to [your role].
ask: How is AI changing the work of a new joiner in my role?
Which businesses (gold, MSME, rural) are the main growth focus after the capital raise?
What does success look like in the first six months?

gd.t: Is easy EMI credit good for young Indians?
gd.for: It lets people buy needed goods and build a credit history.
gd.against: It can lead to over-borrowing and debt stress.

gd.t: Should NBFCs face the same rules as banks?
gd.for: Large NBFCs like Bajaj Finance are as big as banks and affect the whole system.
gd.against: Lighter rules let NBFCs reach borrowers banks ignore.

avoid: Don't say Anup Saha is MD; he resigned in July 2025. Rajeev Jain is Vice Chairman & MD.
Don't mix up Bajaj Finance (the lender) with Bajaj Finserv (its parent holding company) or Bajaj Auto.
Don't mix consolidated (₹19,332 cr) and standalone (₹17,804 cr) FY26 profit; say which one.
